messages:
anya: heads up — nightly perf flagged a regression for torch.compile + CUDA graphs around seqlen ~384-512. ~20% higher P99 on the hot-path compared to last night. repro + traces below. :eyes:

anya: repro (local):
```
PYTHONPATH=./src python -m bench.run_infer --model gpt-3.5-small --seqlen 512 --batch 1 --use-torch-compile --use-cudagraphs --autotune True
```

anya: short profiler excerpt (nvprof-style) — notice the kernel pick changes between seqlen 384 vs 512: 
```
[2026-02-14 03:21:08] KernelPick: arch=sm90 kernel=matmul_tile_32x8_v1 (cost_est=125.4)
[2026-02-14 03:21:09] KernelPick: arch=sm90 kernel=matmul_tile_16x16_v0 (cost_est=98.1)  <-- selected at seqlen=512 (unexpected)
[2026-02-14 03:21:09] Launch: cudagraph_capture(id=42) shapes=(batch=1,seqlen=512,head=32)
[2026-02-14 03:21:10] Latency P99: 72ms (baseline yesterday: 60ms)
```

lina: hmm. is the autotuner picking the 16x16 on purpose? that sounds like the small-tile kernel which usually helps small matmuls but hurts throughput for this head/seq combo. any KV-cache warmup differences?

anya: KV warmup is identical in the bench. I dug into the autotune DB: the pick for 512 came from a single noisy sample when capture happened on a warmup step that included a short prompt (seqlen 32) earlier in the trace; the captured graph fused a different attention kernel shape.

mike: sounds like shape-driven capture boundary (shapecutoff) + torch.compile trace nondeterminism. cudagraph capture can materialize a path with internal tiling tuned to the traced op shapes. if the graph is captured after a short prompt warmup, the autotuner entry maps that capture hash -> kernel choice. later, when actual seqlen=512 runs, we reuse the capture but it runs suboptimally.

tom: can you paste the capture hash / autotune key? We should see if the autotune index uses the capture hash + arch only (and not seqlen bucket).

anya: capture key: gcapture_v2:hash=0x7f9b2a3c; autotune entry: {arch: sm90, key: 0x7f9b2a3c, kernel=matmul_tile_16x16_v0, score=0.92} (score from noisy sample).

lina: ok — immediate fix options:
- invalidate autotune entries that were created during cudagraph capture when traced shapes differ (conservative)
- add seqlen bucket to autotune key so picks are seq-dependent
- prefer arch-aware heuristics override for certain head/hidden combos

mike: quick workaround that helped locally: disable cudagraphs for seqlen range [384,1024] while we sort autotuner. doing `--use-cudagraphs False` in bench goes back to baseline P99. suggests capture reuse is the root cause.

tom: long-term we want: autotune key -> (arch, capture_hash, seqlen_bucket). also add a shadow-run: when we pick a kernel for a captured graph, do one verification run at first use with higher sampling to avoid noisy picks.

engbot: perf-alert created: PERF-2026-1346. nightly impacted jobs: inference-xl-hosted, dedicated-gpu-64. PR checklist suggested in alert.

anya: I started a tiny reproducer and a unit test that simulates capture after a short prompt and then runs long sequences to verify autotune stability. will send PR in a bit.

mike: one more datapoint: on Ampere-class (sm86) the autotuner picks the 32x8 and no regression. it's only on sm90 where our kernel performance cross-over is near 480-520 seqlen. so make the autotuner architecture-aware (weight arch more heavily than noisy sample score).

lina: agreed. action items:
- anya: open PR with test + frag that disables cudagraphs for the failing bucket + quick revert plan (ETA today)
- tom: change autotune key schema to include seqlen_bucket and arch ordering, add verification shadow run (ETA 2 days)
- mike: run cross-arch nightly job to record kernel cross-over points and dump to autotune policy (ETA 3 days)

anya: created draft PR: https://git.redwood/infra/bench/pulls/312 (WIP) — includes reproducer and unit test.

tom: thanks — also add a note to rollout: if we flip autotune schema we need a migration path for existing entries (invalidate best-effort) to avoid flipping live behavior unexpectedly.

mike: +1. also add a perf test in our canary suite that runs 512/384 pairs and asserts P99 within 10% of baseline so we catch regressions early.

lina: :thumbsup: OK let's track PERF-2026-1346 here and sync tomorrow 10am PT if anyone wants to triage together.

anya: thanks all, will post updates in the PR and link back here. :rocket:
